Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 25-30 y/o female with first episode of severe 3-day continuous right-predominant headache with photophobia and transient visual “shooting lights”; most consistent with migraine with visual aura, but serious secondary causes require exclusion.

History:
- Presenting complaint: “Blinding” headache for 3 days, began suddenly on waking; constant 8/10 → 5/10 after ibuprofen, never fully resolves.
- Location/character: Diffuse, worst over right eye; worsens with bright light and sudden standing/head movement; partially improves with ibuprofen; not waking her from sleep.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia, transient visual light flashes; mild nausea; no vomiting, fever, neck stiffness, focal neuro symptoms, sinus/respiratory symptoms, smell/taste change.
- Pertinent negatives: No limb weakness/numbness, speech difficulty, weight change, trauma.
- PMH: None significant.
- Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (started 1 yr ago, brand not recalled); PRN ibuprofen.
- Allergies: None.
- Family history: Mother with migraines with vomiting.
- Social / preventive: Lives alone, works from home; non-smoker; alcohol ~3 drinks once a week; no recreational drug use; no recent travel. Last BP check 1 yr ago “normal.”

Examination:
- Tele-visit only; no vitals taken.
- Patient afebrile by history.
- No physical or neurologic exam performed yet.

Impression:
- Most likely: Migraine with visual aura (photophobia, visual phenomena, unilateral severity, family history, partial NSAID response).
- Need to rule out:
  • Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (female, estrogen OCP, positional element, persistent severe pain).  
  • Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (young woman, visual symptoms; fundoscopic exam pending).
- No current evidence of meningitis, subarachnoid hemorrhage, or sinusitis, but advise urgent evaluation if symptoms escalate.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person appointment for full neurologic examination, including BP measurement and fundoscopy.
- Prescribe stronger NSAID (exact drug not specified in transcript) plus concurrent acetaminophen; instruct to take with food.
- Continue current OCP for now; advise that pill may need change if migraine with aura confirmed.
- Safety-net advice: If headache becomes unbearable, changes in character, or new neurologic signs develop, go to Emergency Department or call service immediately.
- Cancel follow-up visit if symptoms completely resolve before appointment.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected: Objective vitals (BP, HR, temp), full neuro & fundoscopy findings, exact NSAID prescription details, brand name of OCP, specific follow-up timeframe/date.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear but minor audio gaps; no demographic details recorded in transcript; no physical exam possible in tele-visit.
